housing.text: Schultz says he is working to make it easier to build housing and supported legislation allowing some commercial properties to be converted to residential use.
housing.quote: Nick is fighting to make it easier to build needed housing and expand programs to help renters and first-time homebuyers.

schools.text: Schultz says he supports fully funding public education and has backed increased school funding and teacher-support programs.
schools.quote: Local teachers support Nick because he’s a champion for fully funding our system of public education and lowering barriers for college students.

sentencing.text: As committee chair, Schultz recommended voting yes on a bill that would allow courts to impose an additional sentencing aggravating factor.

immigration.text: Schultz co-authored legislation limiting immigration enforcement access to schools without a judicial warrant and requiring notification when enforcement occurs on campus.
immigration.quote: AB 49, which prohibits employees of a local education agency from allowing immigration enforcement to enter a school site without a valid judicial warrant or court order

energy.text: Schultz authored a bill intended to reduce electricity costs for consumers and said he would revise and reintroduce it after the governor’s veto.
energy.quote: Had it passed, the bill would have significantly decreased energy costs for consumers and retail rate payers – up to $550 million a year, according to Schultz.

tax.text: She supports suspending the gas tax, cutting the car tax and reducing income taxes while opposing new tax hikes.
tax.quote: Suspend the gas tax, cut the car tax, and reduce the income tax. Defend Prop. 13.

housing.text: She supports cutting regulations and streamlining permits to increase the housing supply.
housing.quote: Build More Homes: Cut expensive regulations and streamline permitting to increase supply.

safety.text: She supports police, Prop. 36 reforms and prioritizing victims in public-safety policy.
safety.quote: Restore Public Safety: Support Prop. 36 reforms, back police, and put victims first—not criminals.

sentencing.text: She supports incarcerating drug offenders and enforcing anti-camping laws.
sentencing.quote: Prioritize mental treatment and incarcerate drug offenders. Enforce anti-camping laws.

energy.text: She supports expanding access to natural resources and reducing climate policies that she says raise energy costs.
energy.quote: Reduce Energy Bills: California has plenty of natural resources. Sacramento is blocking them. Dump foolish climate policies and make energy abundant again.
